description: A-BOA\*ε is an anytime search for two objectives: it reports a better approximation of the Pareto front each time it finds one. It keeps the solutions found so far as the corners of *intervals*, and each interval holds the paths that can still give a new solution between its two corners. The *approximation factor* `ε̂` of an interval tells how far its corners can be from such a solution. Each iteration takes the interval with the largest `ε̂`, runs BOA\*ε on its paths with `ε = ε̂ / d`, and keeps the paths that only the tolerance pruned for later iterations, so no work repeats. The reported factors fall strictly, and a complete run ends with the exact front; the crate also has a weighted-sum pruning variant and a baseline that restarts every iteration.

papers.authors: Han Zhang, Oren Salzman, T. K. Satish Kumar, Ariel Felner, Carlos Hernández Ulloa, Sven Koenig
papers.title: Anytime Approximate Bi-Objective Search
